title: Service Access Envelope: terraform module for permission profiles and binding hygiene
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: deliver a reusable Terraform module (service-access-envelope) that provides opinionated least-privilege IAM/RBAC profiles, binding templates, and safety checks for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. The module should: 1) produce composable permission envelopes for common runtime roles (control-plane, model-executor, metrics-ingest, storage-proxy), 2) offer binding templates per cloud provider (IAM role, service account, role-binding) and per target (k8s service account, compute instance), 3) include upgrade and migration hooks so operators can roll from broad legacy policies to scoped envelopes with minimal downtime, and 4) surface automated health checks and drift detection for IAM bindings with optional automatic remediation or alerting.

Why this ticket: current private deployment onboarding requires multiple hand-crafted TF files per customer and ad-hoc permissive bindings. This module will standardize the surface, reduce human error, and provide a safer upgrade path for existing customers to narrow permissions over time. It also enables programmatic policy attestation for audits and integrates with our upgrade playbooks.

Design notes / constraints: - The module must be provider-agnostic at the API-level (inputs to describe principals and permission-sets) while providing concrete sub-modules for aws/gcp/azure where provider blocks diverge. - Keep surface minimal: inputs = env (dev/stage/prod), role_family (e.g., model-executor), permission_tier (read-only, exec, admin-lite), allowed_resources (pattern list), tags and cost-center. - Emit metadata outputs for telemetry (policy_hash, binding_count, last_applied_by, module_version). - Include a lightweight terraforming plan generator to produce recommended narrow policies from an existing permissive principal (migration helper). - All code must pass static checks and terratest suites; examples for k8s and VM-based deploys required.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable terraform module named 'service-access-envelope' exists in terraform/priv-iam/ with clear README and examples for aws/gcp/azure
Module exposes inputs for env, role_family, permission_tier, allowed_resources, principal_type and outputs telemetry fields (policy_hash, binding_count, last_applied_by)
Provider-specific sub-modules (aws/gcp/azure) implement binding templates: IAM role, service account, role-binding and include minimal inline policy generation and tagging
Migration helper script (terraform plan generator) can take an existing broad principal and output a recommended narrow policy diff for review
Module has automated CI terratest and staticcheck jobs that run for examples and provider mocks
Health checks: drift detector runs (via CI or scheduled job) and reports to infra-observability dashboard; optional remediation flag documented
Documentation includes an 'upgrade playbook' with step-by-step rollback-safe narrowing process and sample approval checklist for customers
Security review completed and checklist items tracked in the ticket; no high-risk findings outstanding
At least two customer onboarding examples (one GCP k8s, one AWS instance-profile) are validated in internal staging
